mem.root_cause:
The extra memory comes from two causes that add up. rsvelte triggers one full program build per shadow, and tsrs keeps part of every full build after the program is freed.

1) rsvelte cause: diskless shadows plus eager didOpen cause one full rebuild per shadow. rsvelte_language_server keeps every .svelte.tsx shadow body in memory only (tsgo_overlay.rs:1-6; ensure_shadow_parent at tsgo_overlay.rs:1338-1343 even refuses a body that exists on disk). It makes the shadows visible to TS by didOpen-ing every eager shadow at startup: TsgoRuntime::start at server.rs:536, ensure_overlay_for at ~598, rebuild_tsgo_overlays at 2576. The overlay tsconfig's root set comes from disk: write_tsconfig at tsgo_overlay.rs:1243 has `include: ["svelte/**/*"]` over a directory that holds no bodies. tsgo/tsrs therefore treat each didOpen of a file that is not on disk as a file creation that matches the config's include. Each one logs "Checking if any of 1 created files match root files" → "Root files for config ... changed" → "Reloading file names for config", then a full CreateProgram ("Program update ... 10-25 ms"; it is not ReuseProgram). It also publishes the config's project diagnostics; those are the 166/332 empty publishDiagnostics, all for tsconfig.json.
- N shadows give N full builds. That is 166 for admin/src, 332 for admin and 476 for the repo root (12 projects).
- The opens alone take 3.2 s (admin/src) to about 8 s of tsrs time, which is most of the 3-15 s first-diagnostic latency.

2) tsrs cause: tsrs keeps memory after every full program build. tsgo's GC frees superseded builds. tsrs frees the program owners: TSRS_REGION_LOG shows created/freed pairs, 169/168. Even so, it keeps about 360 B per program file plus about 70 B per import per full build. On zeno/admin/src that is about 1.3 MB per rebuild, and about 2.2 MB per diskless didOpen. It is split roughly evenly between the arena reservation and the mimalloc heap, and it is never returned. ReuseProgram (content-only edits) does not leak. So 166 opens leave about 360 MB behind: 87 → 446 MB before the first pull. The first diagnostic pull itself adds only about 2 MB.

3) Duplicate Node-only project. When the workspace is admin/, replayed_shadows (server.rs:435-452) replays every eager shadow of an overlay that has its own tsconfig (`overlay.source_tsconfig().is_some() || ...`). That includes all 166 shadows that the nested admin/src project serves. The Node-only admin/tsconfig.json project (types: node, no DOM) gets a second full program and a second rebuild storm, even though it serves no .svelte document. Every .svelte file under admin/ is inside admin/src.

Things that make no difference, all tested by replay:
- initializationOptions and inlay-hint settings, and the workspace/configuration answers (replacing them with null still gives 464 MB).
- didChangeWatchedFiles: none were sent.
- The diagnostic pulls (+2 MB).
- The shims, which are byte-identical to svelte_check's.
- The overlay's paths/rootDirs/typeRoots. With bodies on disk, a CLI full check of rsvelte's overlay is 1000 files / 163 MB, against 1214 files / 166 MB for svelte_check's overlay.
- Removing the include glob does not help: 567 MB, 239 programs. Listing all shadows in "files" does not help either: 497 MB, 169 programs.

Only having the bodies on disk removes the rebuilds.

mem.risks:
- **Disk writes.** Roughly 2.5-5 KB per component: 166 files (866 KB) for admin/src, about 480 at the root. They happen once per change because writes are skipped when content is unchanged.
- **Stale bodies.** Bodies from deleted or renamed sources would become phantom root files through svelte/**/*. Mitigations: delete them in remove_source, sweep at build time, and rename atomically (temp names end in .tmp, which the include glob ignores).
- **Concurrent sessions.** Two sessions on one workspace write identical content atomically.
- **Upstream rsvelte on the same workspace.** It would refuse our bodies because of its diskless check in ensure_shadow_parent. A separate cache directory name avoids this.
- **Watchers.** rsvelte answers tsgo's registerCapability with null, and Zed only watches the globs rsvelte registers, so writing bodies produces no watch events.
- **Unsaved buffers.** Editor text stays in the tsgo overlay; disk holds the saved-source projection, and the overlay wins.
- **Preprocessed projects** (shadcn-rhea): persist the preprocessed projection, or the first didChange becomes one batched rebuild.
- **Step 2 (replay only from the serving overlay).** An outer configured project loses nested shadows as open buffers. With bodies on disk, it still sees the ones its own overlay persists. Upstream svelte-language-server never serves those documents from the outer project either.
- **Step 3 (lazy open)** depends on the synthetic didChangeWatchedFiles reaching tsgo for changes to closed components; test this explicitly, and test crash-restart replay too.
- **Tests that assert disklessness** must be rewritten.
- **Measurement interference.** The scratchpad is shared, and another agent's cleanup deleted my relocated test bodies once. I recreated them inside the lock, and the earlier disk results are confirmed by their publish counts (1 or 2 per run, against 166/332 diskless). lat.root_cause:
The first-open latency comes almost entirely from tsrs working through shadow didOpens one at a time. Only about 10% of it is in the svelte-rs server.

1. rsvelte keeps the shadow of every closed component in tsrs as an in-memory open document. At startup it sends them as one `textDocument/didOpen` each, before the first diagnostic request:
   - `server.rs:536-543` (`TsgoRuntime::start` → `client.open_buffer`)
   - `tsgo_client.rs:604-608` (supervisor replays `state.buffers` in URI order)
   - Counts: 476 shadows (1.69 MB of text, 1.98 MB as JSON) at the repo root; 332 at workspace=admin; 166 at admin/src.

2. tsrs (a port of tsgo) handles notifications strictly in order in one dispatch loop (`tsrs_lsp/src/server.rs:1358` `dispatch_loop`).
   - `did_open_file` (`tsrs_project/src/session.rs:343`) clones the snapshot immediately, with the opened document as a requested resource.
   - The shadow is not on disk but matches the overlay tsconfig's `"svelte/**/*"` include (`tsgo_overlay.rs:1243`). So every open counts as a created root file: "Root files for config … changed" → "Reloading file names for config" (about 3 ms) → full "Program update" for that project (10–20 ms with about 970 files).
   - Over the 476 opens: 481 snapshot clones (7.86 s), 464 config reloads, 479 program rebuilds (5.88 s; admin/src alone is 169 × 16.4 ms = 2.78 s). All 12 component projects get loaded, so tsrs grows to about 950 MB.
   - The editor's diagnostic pull is queued behind all of them. The pull itself takes 6–13 ms. There is no fixed delay in tsrs.

3. The "~1.5 s per pull" in `bench/spike-opencount.mjs` is a bug in that script. Lines 17-20 time `await s.pull(target); await sleep(1500);` together, so the 1.5 s is the script's own sleep.

4. workspace=admin replays every component twice, once into the admin/tsconfig.json (node) project and once into admin/src. `replayed_shadows` (`server.rs:435-453`) replays every shadow of any overlay that has a tsconfig, even when a nearer config owns the file. That is why 6.8 s is about 2 × 3.3 s.

5. Server-side critical path:
   - `initialize` blocks for about 630 ms (`server.rs:150`, `TsgoRuntime::start` runs before `initialize_finish`). The root overlay walks the whole repo (119 ms) and projects all 476 components (261 ms). The 12 nested overlays project the same 476 components again (about 245 ms). tsrs is spawned only after all of this.
   - On the first didOpen, `queue_preprocess_document` → `ensure_preprocess_runtime` → `preprocess_inputs` blocks the main loop for 231 ms. `find_preprocess_config` (`preprocess_sidecar.rs:730`) canonicalizes 5 config names at every directory level for each of the 952 eager shadows.
   - When a workspace has no svelte.config (admin, admin/src), the empty result is never remembered, so the same scan (65–70 ms) runs on every didOpen and didChange. That makes edits at workspace=admin take 84–92 ms.

6. Overlay cache writes are not a cost.
   - Cold cache: 53 files (13 overlays × 3 shims + tsconfig, plus .gitignore) and about 408 dirs.
   - Warm start: `write_if_changed` rewrites 0 files (mtimes stayed at 19:44 through all my runs). There are still 952 `create_dir_all` calls plus symlink checks, which are counted inside the projection time.

At startup the server loads every project eagerly and assigns components to projects by directory. Both choices together cause the slow first open and the high memory.

1. TsgoRuntime::start (vendor/rsvelte/crates/rsvelte_language_server/src/server.rs:468-551) runs before `initialize` is answered:

   - That overlay's discover_sources (tsgo_overlay.rs:724-756) projects every .svelte file under the folder (`find_svelte_files`).
   - add_nested_overlays (server.rs:413-428, fed by nested_project_configs 397-411; called at :512) then builds one more overlay for every tsconfig.json/jsconfig.json that is the nearest config of any .svelte file. Each of these again projects every .svelte file under its own directory, plus a closure that follows relative imports only.
   - replayed_shadows (server.rs:435-453; loop at :536) then sends textDocument/didOpen to tsrs for every one of those shadows.
   - Project membership is "every .svelte below the project directory", not "documents whose nearest config is this one". So with workspace=admin, the Node-only admin/tsconfig.json project (include: vite.config.ts and vitest.config.ts) also receives all 166 admin/src components that admin/src/tsconfig.json already owns.

2. tsrs pays a cost on every opened shadow, and that cost grows with the size of the project. tsrs_project session.rs:343 `did_open_file` (a port of tsgo session.go:319) updates the snapshot synchronously on each didOpen. tsrs logs show, per open shadow:
   - "Root files for config … changed"
   - "Reloading file names for config" (about 3 ms)
   - "Program update … completed in ~18 ms" for the ~800-file admin/src program.
   Notifications are handled one at a time, so the editor's first diagnostic request waits behind every replayed open (476 at the zeno root), whichever project the user actually opened.

3. Related costs that appear once loading is lazy:
   - **Every watched-file event:** any event refreshes all overlays (refresh_tsgo_overlays, server.rs:2520), which re-walks the directories and re-reads every shadowed .svelte file. tsrs registers `zeno/**/*` watchers, so the editor reports essentially every file change.
   - **Overlay config writes:** a write to an overlay's own `.rsvelte-language-server/**/tsconfig.json` matches is_project_config (server.rs:4479) and triggers rebuild_tsgo_overlays plus a tsgo restart. This, not tsgo itself, is the real hazard behind the comment at server.rs:506-511. tsrs logs show that creating a new project marks only that project dirty.
   - **Every keystroke:** queue_preprocess_document (server.rs:2757) calls ensure_preprocess_runtime, which recomputes preprocess_inputs (2712-2755) over all shadows on every didOpen and didChange while no preprocess sidecar is running. At the eager zeno root this is hidden only because playground/shadcn-rhea happens to start the sidecar.
   - **Owner vs. copy:** the lookups that answer "which shadow belongs to this source" pick the deepest overlay (tsgo_response.rs:1182) or the first one found (server.rs:1229, 1308, 1615). Neither can tell the owning project from another project's copy of the same component. Lazy loading makes such copies common.

4. Cross-project resolution works like this. A component is resolvable only inside one tsgo project:
   - Its shadow must be open at `<cache>/svelte/<path relative to the mirror root>.svelte.tsx` in that project's own shadow directory, and the parent directory must exist on disk.
   - Specifiers ending in .svelte get `.tsx` appended (rewrite_plain_svelte_imports, tsgo_overlay.rs:1970).
   - Relative imports from source files on disk reach the shadows through `rootDirs [mirror_root, shadow_dir]`.
   - `paths` and baseUrl targets get a twin entry pointing into the shadow tree (overlay_paths, tsgo_overlay.rs:1163-1228).
   - The unresolved-route invariants are ShadowResolutionInfo::is_resolvable (tsgo_overlay.rs:81).
   - Consequence: projects never resolve into another project's shadow tree. So loading project P never requires loading another project Q in tsgo. P only needs its own copies of Q components that P can reach.

**What could break and how to catch it:**
- Workspace symbols, references and rename now cover only loaded projects. This matches upstream. Document it, and consider the opt-in loadAllProjects setting.
- The first request in a project that is not loaded yet pays that project's load (1–4 s in zeno). Project builds run on the main loop (30–150 ms). They could later move to the worker.
- A .svelte file reached only through a package import, such as a node_modules symlink with an `exports` entry pointing at .svelte, is still not followed. Same as today.
- Closure copies resolve their own imports with the importing project's `paths`, as today's relative closure does.
- **Updating copies on every keystroke:** projection cost is multiplied by the number of copies, usually 0–1.
- **Ownership must win everywhere:** any lookup still using `find_map` or depth only can route requests to a copy. That failure was reproduced (step C5).
- **Watch events:** filtering `.rsvelte-language-server` out of rsvelte's own config detection must not stop forwarding those events to tsgo, which relies on directory-creation events.
- **Changed membership:** a root that has its own tsconfig no longer shadows documents that a nested config owns. Only the root project's own references to them change, and imports are still covered by the closure.
- **Lazy builds after tsgo starts:** the order of writes before didOpen matters. tsrs logs show no reload of other projects. Covered by the integration tests below.
